options.rationale: Correct: angles in a triangle sum to 180, and 180 - 50 - 60 = 70.

That would make the sum 170, not 180.

items.stem: Select TWO facts that are always true. (Select TWO.)

options.text: Angles on a straight line add up to 180 degrees
options.rationale: Correct: a straight line is a half turn, 180 degrees.

options.text: Angles around a point add up to 360 degrees
options.rationale: Correct: a full turn around a point is 360 degrees.

options.text: Every triangle has a right angle
options.rationale: Only right-angled triangles do; many triangles have none.

options.text: All angles in a quadrilateral are equal
options.rationale: Only some quadrilaterals, like squares, have equal angles.

items.explanation: Correct: a straight line is a half turn, 180 degrees.

options.rationale: Correct: angles on a straight line sum to 180, and 180 - 125 = 55.
That adds the angles; they should total 180.
